articles.title: 2 giant pandas arrive at Zoo Atlanta in a rare loan from China
articles.summary: Two giant pandas on loan from the Chinese government as part of Beijing’s long tradition of “panda diplomacy” have arrived at Zoo Atlanta.
articles.body:
Two giant pandas on loan from the Chinese government as part of Beijing's long tradition of "panda diplomacy" have arrived at Zoo Atlanta.

The pandas — a male named Ping Ping and a female named Fu Shuang — arrived on a FedEx flight Sunday from Chengdu, in southwestern China. They are the third pair of pandas to arrive in the US in the past two years, and their arrival at Zoo Atlanta comes with great fanfare given how rare the bears are in US zoos.

"We are elated to welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and could not be more excited about sharing that joy with our Members, guests, city, and community in the coming weeks," Raymond B. King, president and CEO of Zoo Atlanta, said in a statement.

In 2024, Zoo Atlanta returned four pandas who had lived at the zoo back to China, marking the end of a 25-year agreement between the zoo and China.

As the plane's cargo door opened, CNN's team at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport saw two large crates lowered to the ground and then each loaded onto a FedEx truck. With a police escort, the trucks left the airport for the 10-mile drive to the zoo.

Once at the zoo, the crates — emblazoned with the zoo's logo — were lifted off the trucks by an orange forklift, and the pandas were brought inside to begin their residency in Atlanta.

Visitors to the zoo will have to wait to see the fluffy guests, as the bears will be housed in a biosecure area of Zoo Atlanta's new giant panda complex for a routine quarantine period of about a month, according to the zoo.

The pandas departed Chengdu at 2:55 a.m. Sunday morning local time (2:55 p.m. ET Saturday), China's state news agency Xinhua said. The flight came just a day after Chinese leader Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington concluded.

During that visit, which was intended to address rising US-China tensions, Xi and US President Donald Trump extended a trade truce and agreed to establish an AI hotline between the two countries.

Video from Xinhua showed fans waving placards as trucks carrying the pandas headed to the airport, from the Giant Panda Breeding Research Base in Sichuan province. Vehicles then towed two crates to the plane, and the crates were lifted aboard ahead of the nearly 16-hour journey.

China also arranged for several veterinarians and breeders to remain at the zoo in Atlanta as the pandas enter quarantine upon arrival, the agency added.

The team at Zoo Atlanta and the Chinese team held "many online and offline meetings to carry out in-depth exchanges on the upgrading and transformation plan" for the venue that houses the pandas, which will be on loan from the Chinese government, according to Xinhua.

"What Zoo Atlanta has been working hard for the past year is making improvements to our enclosures, where our enclosures are a lot bigger," Sam Rivera, the zoo's vice president of animal health, told Xinhua. "We're ensuring that we have plenty of bamboo for them to eat. We have experienced keepers that are trained on taking care of giant pandas."

Rare, fluffy and irresistibly cute, pandas are adored across the globe. The animals once roamed a vast swath of China, along with parts of northern Myanmar and Vietnam, but human encroachment and climate change shrank the habitat of the bamboo-munching bears to just six mountain ranges above the Sichuan basin, deep in China's hinterland.

Hailed in imperial times as the "land of heavenly abundance," Sichuan is now better known as the "hometown of pandas." The mountainous province boasts a latticework of panda nature reserves and breeding centers, all built in recent decades as China – and the world – raced to save the multimillion-years-old "living fossil" from extinction.

Provincial capital Chengdu – a sprawling metropolis known for its spicy hotpot and old tea houses – sits at the foot of snow-capped mountains with misty old-growth forests where wild pandas still roam.

The city's panda breeding base is the largest in the country, housing more than 240 bears – or a third of the world's captive panda population. The sprawling facility draws up to 11 million visitors a year, on par with Shanghai Disneyland.

Loaning pandas has long been a tool of Chinese diplomacy, following a decades-long government effort to transform them from a little-known animal into a cultural icon and national symbol. For more than half a century, Beijing has dispatched these charismatic animals overseas to shore up alliances, mend estranged ties and court new partners.

"The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and Americans," Xi said on Thursday , referencing the half-century in which pandas lived in US zoos on loan from the Chinese government. That tradition was started by Chairman Mao Zedong in 1972, shortly after Richard Nixon became the first US president to visit China following the Communist Party's rise to power in 1949.

One of the pandas bound for Atlanta even has the same name – Ping Ping, meaning "peace" – as the first ever panda Mao gifted to the Soviet Union in 1957. He was born on March 17, 2020, has large black patches around his eyes and is especially good at climbing trees, according to China's National Forestry and Grassland Administration.

The other panda, Fu Shuang, meaning "double blessings," was born seven months later on October 18. She has a small tuft of fur on the top of her head, a slightly protruding forehead and finds food very easily, the administration said.

In a report ahead of their journey, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV asked their keeper to describe the pair.

Ping Ping "is brave and gentle," Fu Jia said. "During training sessions, when he spots me holding an apple, he will make soft whimpering sounds, eager for the treat."

Fu Shuang, on the other hand, "is crazy about honey," she said.

Zookeepers at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding selected the pair after considering their age, health, genetics and personality.

"They should be docile and like each other, and hopefully be able to mate naturally," the park's deputy director Li Mingxi told Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

The zoo has hosted several pandas before. Another pair, Lun Lun and Yang Yang, had seven offspring there between 2006 and 2016 before returning to Chengdu.

Zoo Atlanta earlier in the year said it would be "delighted and honored" to welcome the two pandas.

A banner displayed at the zoo on Saturday read "The future home of Ping Ping and Fu Shuang."

Chinese officials and the Atlanta zoo "will carry out in-depth academic and cultural exchanges to continuously enhance mutual understanding and friendship between the people of China and the United States," Xinhua said.

Panda diplomacy has offered some relief from the tensions increasingly shaping the US-China relationship in recent years, as the two countries compete in an AI arms race and engage in a spiraling trade war.

Two giant pandas arrived in San Diego in June 2024, the first time China allowed new pandas to travel to the US in more than two decades. A second pair traveled to Washington's National Zoo later that year.

In preparation for the move, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang have been quarantined for a month with a roster of live-in carers, Li said. The pandas have been trained for their long flight too, becoming used to their crate and loud noises.

Late Saturday night, China's ambassador to the US Xie Feng shared photos of the two pandas on his X account and said they were on their way.

"Get ready to greet our two fluffy stars!" he wrote.

Their departure would be a sad one for, Fu, their keeper.

"After caring for them for so long… It's like raising your own children," she told CCTV.

"They weighed barely over 100 grams at birth, and we nurtured them until they grew big and heavy. I won't get to see them for quite a long time, so it's hard to say goodbye."

CNN's Xiaoqian Lin, Farida Elsebai, Rebekah Riess, Eduardo Cuevas , Mitchell McCluskey and Shawn Nottingham contributed reporting.

articles.title: Electric barriers replace manual gates on key Chennai rail routes
articles.summary: Chennai Division upgrades rail level crossings: 70 of 143 now have electric lifting barriers, cutting closure time to 8–12 seconds; 133 get emergency booms.
articles.body: Chennai: A level-crossing that once took a gatekeeper up to three minutes to open or close can now be cleared in about eight to 12 seconds as Chennai Division of Southern Railway steps up the replacement of manual barriers with electrically operated systems. Of the 143 manned level crossings in the division, 70 have been converted to electrically operated lifting barriers (EOLBs).The conversion is aimed at reducing the time road users wait at crossings and preventing vehicles from attempting to pass through barriers while they are being operated manually. Each EOLB unit costs about ₹30 lakh.Chennai Beach-Chengalpet section has achieved complete coverage, with all 13 manned level crossings such as Chromepet, Pallavaram, Perungalathur and Singaperumal Koil fitted with EOLBs. On Chengalpet-Arakkonam section, 19 of 31 crossings have been converted, while 11 of 29 crossings on Chennai Central-Gudur section have been covered.On other routes, eight of 10 crossings between Chennai Central and Arakkonam have also been upgraded, along with seven of nine between Arakkonam and Katpadi and six of 14 between Arakkonam and Renigunta. Three of eight crossings on Katpadi-Villupuram section and three of 29 on Chengalpet-Villupuram section have also been converted.The remaining crossings will be taken up in phases based on road and rail traffic volumes. Officials also said the faster operation also reduces the scope for road vehicles to damage barriers or cross before they are fully closed. Manual barriers are operated by gatekeepers using hand-cranked winches.As an additional safety measure, Southern Railway has also installed Emergency Sliding Booms at 133 of the 143 crossings. articles.title: ‘They wanted everything up front’: Trump’s UN envoy says Iran was not negotiating in good faith to end war
articles.summary: US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to end the ongoing conflict because Tehran
articles.body: US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to end the ongoing conflict because Tehran wanted sanctions relief and other concessions before negotiations on its nuclear programme.“They were asking for everything up front,” Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday. He said Iran was seeking relief from “billions and billions” of dollars in sanctions before agreeing to negotiate an end to its nuclear programme.Waltz said Trump was not convinced that Iran was negotiating in good faith. He also argued that Tehran’s proposal was unacceptable because it sought major concessions before substantive talks could begin.Trump on Saturday confirmed that he had rejected the Iranian proposal. According to Politico, the plan called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and a resumption of nuclear talks in return for the US lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports, easing sanctions on Iranian oil sales and agreeing to a seven-day ceasefire.“They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump told reporters. He also claimed that the US was “winning tremendously” and had “total control” of the Strait of Hormuz.Iran has disputed the US account. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran remained open to diplomacy but insisted that any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would depend on Tehran meeting its conditions.Speaking on NBC’s Meet the Press, Araghchi said Iran was prepared to resume fighting if necessary but had not abandoned the possibility of negotiations.“We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed,” he said, while adding that Iran remained ready for diplomacy.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also said his country was prepared to hold talks over its nuclear programme and other issues, but would not accept what he described as “bullying or coercion”.The dispute comes amid tensions over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global shipping route, and continued US-Iran military hostilities.Waltz also rejected reports that Trump had decided to resume bombing Iran after the November midterm elections, saying the president had not personally made such a commitment and would keep his options open.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pope Leo calls out ‘false compassion’ of medically assisted suicide during French hospital visit
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned assisted suicide as "false compassion" during a Mass in Lourdes, France, urging the healthcare community to reject causing death.
articles.body: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 800-273-TALK (8255). Pope Leo XIV called for an end to medically assisted suicide during a visit to medical facilities in Lourdes, France, on Sunday. The pope gave Mass in Lourdes before addressing a large crowd who cheered as he emphatically affirmed the dignity of all human lives and admonished listeners to reject the "false compassion" of assisted suicide. POPE LEO XIV BEGINS HISTORIC 4-DAY VISIT TO FRANCE "It is precisely in the name of this inalienable dignity of the human person that we must reject the temptation to cause death under the guise of false compassion," the pope said, speaking in French. "It is impossible to regard causing death as something normal. What is legal is not necessarily moral," he continued. "Here in Lourdes, the city of the sick and of hope, I appeal to the entire healthcare community to remember the profound meaning of your vocation, which is to care for a suffering person, not to eliminate that person." CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH "No one ever has the right based on laboratory algorithms to decide the life of a given embryo or elderly person. Medicine must never become the servant of programmed death," he said. Assisted suicide is legal in many Western countries, including France. MICHIGAN DEMOCRATS PROPOSE PACKAGE SEEKING TO LEGALIZE ASSISTED SUICIDE The practice has come under heavy criticism, particularly in Canada where it has seen widespread use. Last week, the family of an 83-year-old Canadian woman demanded answers after she died through the country's medical assistance in dying program despite allegedly becoming distraught when told the procedure would end her life. ASSISTED LIVING CENTER SENT RESIDENT TO DOCTOR'S APPOINTMENT AFTER GIVING HIM 18 SHOTS, 5 AM BEER: OFFICIALS The Daily Mail reported that 83-year-old Christian grandmother Brigitte Stegemann was killed under Canada’s physician-assisted suicide program, called Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID), on July 10. Her granddaughter, Brigitte Kranendonk, said that she was her grandmother’s primary caregiver and that her family had decided to place Stegemann at The Pearl care home in Cannifton due to physical and mental decline. ORGAN HARVESTING BEGAN WHILE PATIENTS STILL SHOWED ‘SIGNS OF LIFE,’ FEDERAL INVESTIGATION FINDS But according to Kranendonk, her grandmother still had a good appetite even following a stomach cancer diagnosis, and rejected the idea of using MAID when it was presented as an option. Kranendonk said she was present for Stegemann's second MAID assessment, and said that the doctor used "really loose terms, never using the words death or dying." NEW YORK NUNS' CHALLENGE TO ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW IS ABOUT PROTECTING FREEDOM, LAWYER SAYS "She explains MAID to my grandmother by saying: 'We’re going to give you medicine, you’re going to feel at peace. And I just want you to know that you won’t have a bowel movement,'" Kranendonk said. When Kranendonk interjected and said, "She doesn’t understand what you’re saying," the doctor allegedly looked at Stegemann and said, "We’re going to make sure you won’t have any more pain." CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND According to a doctor, Stegemann was "deemed fit for MAID, and we're going to proceed," The Daily Mail reported. Kranendonk said that two days before Stegemann's death, she asked her grandmother directly whether she understood that the scheduled procedure meant she would die. According to Kranendonk's account to the outlet, Stegemann began crying and said she had "made a mistake." articles.title: ‘Damodar, Adi Ganga Among 17 Polluted Rivers’
articles.summary: CPCB flags 17 West Bengal rivers, including Adi Ganga and Damodar, with critically polluted stretches; high BOD and low oxygen linked to sewage and low flows.
articles.body: Kolkata: The Adi Ganga flowing through Kolkata today offers perhaps the starkest snapshot of Bengal’s river crisis. It is among 17 rivers in the state that have critically-polluted stretches, according to the latest Central Pollution Control Board assessment.These rivers are Hooghly, Churni, Damodar, Jalangi, Mathabhanga, Barakar, Dwarakeshwar, Dwarka, Rupnarayan, Teesta, Bidyadhari, Kansi, Silabati, Kalijani, Mayurakshi and Karola. At Jirat Bridge, a West Bengal Pollution Control Board sample collected in Nov last year had found the water blackish and foul-smelling, with biochemical oxygen demand at 18.5 mg/l, dissolved oxygen at just 2 mg/l and faecal coliform at a staggering 84 lakh MPN per 100 ml.On World Rivers Day, numbers show that many of Bengal’s rivers continue to suffer from sewage discharge, organic pollution, shrinking flows and pressure from urbanisation. CPCB data show particularly serious organic pollution in stretches of the Mahananda, Bidyadhari and Churni.The Hooghly itself has a polluted stretch extending from Berhampore to Haldia, while the Churni stretch from Bijoypur to Ranaghat recorded a maximum BOD of 20.8 mg/l in the CPCB assessment. The Vidyadhari stretch between Haroa and Malancha recorded 29.6 mg/l, and the Mahananda near Siliguri 31 mg/l.“High BOD means the water contains a heavy load of organic pollutants, while low dissolved oxygen shows that the river is losing its capacity to sustain aquatic life. The situation becomes particularly severe during the lean season, when natural flow is low and there is not enough water to dilute the sewage entering the river. If untreated or inadequately treated sewage continues to dominate the flow, a river gradually loses its ecological character and begins to function more like a wastewater channel,” said river scientist Kalyan Rudra. Adi Ganga and the city’s canal network receive enormous wastewater loads, while restoration projects have struggled to keep pace with population growth and urban expansion. Experts say Bengal’s rivers are also losing their ecological resilience because of encroachment, siltation, altered channels, reduced dry-season flows and shrinking floodplains.“Treating sewage is necessary, but it cannot by itself revive a river. A river needs adequate ecological flow, space for its floodplain and protection from encroachment, waste dumping and indiscriminate construction along its banks. If we clean the sewage but continue to choke the river’s natural course and destroy its floodplain, restoration will remain incomplete. Bengal needs to treat rivers as living ecosystems, not just drains that have to be cleaned,” said Naba Dutta, general secretary of Sabuj Mancha, which has launched a state-wide movement for revival of rivers.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Nepal: 16 feared dead after avalanche buries Himlung Himal base camp under 15ft snow
articles.summary: Sixteen expedition support staff are feared dead after an avalanche buried tents at Himlung Himal (7,126m) base camp in Nepal’s Manang district under more
articles.body: Sixteen expedition support staff are feared dead after an avalanche buried tents at Himlung Himal (7,126m) base camp in Nepal’s Manang district under more than 15ft of snow on Sunday morning. Rescuers recovered two bodies while 14 others, mostly kitchen staff, remained missing. Search teams said chances of finding survivors were slim. Operations were suspended later in the day due to difficult conditions and were scheduled to resume Monday morning.Members of the search and rescue team identified the two deceased as climbing guides Pasang Bhote and Chhebi Bhote. “We will resume the search for the 14 other kitchen staff,” Mingma G Sherpa, who led the rescue operation, told TOI. The avalanche struck while a Himalayan Holidays Nepal team was preparing the base camp for a 14-member all-women group from a climbing school in the UAE, scheduled to arrive in Kathmandu on Oct 1.Himlung Himal, in the Nar Phu region of Manang, had witnessed persistent rain and heavy snowfall before the avalanche. At least eight IFMGA/NNMGA guides were mobilised for the rescue, but poor weather restricted access to the base camp. “It is very unlikely that the missing people will be found alive, as the tents were buried beneath more than 15ft of snow,” rescuers involved in recovering the bodies said.Nepal's department of tourism said 14 staff from Himalayan Holidays and two kitchen workers from Imagine Nepal Treks were caught in the avalanche. Initial reports had put the number of missing people lower before expedition organisers and authorities revised the figure after receiving details from the remote site.The accident came amid a deadly 2026 climbing season across Himalayas and Karakoram, where at least 24 climbers and high-altitude workers had already died before Sunday’s incident. The toll included fatalities during Nepal’s spring season, an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakista-occupied Kashmir n and four deaths on Manaslu this month.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Bihar tourism makeover: Govt to use AI, digital tech and heli-tourism; Rs1,301 crore projects approved as major temple corridors and new facilities progress.
articles.body: Patna: Govt is planning a makeover of the tourism sector, with AI, digital technology and heli-tourism.Speaking at a function on World Tourism Day on Sunday, tourism minister Kedar Prasad Gupta said AI and technology would be important for tourism. He said the state govt, under the leadership of CM Samrat Choudhary, was linking tourism with development, employment and economy.Bihar recorded more than 6.62 crore arrivals in 2025. Projects worth Rs1,301 crore were approved in 2025-26, while 36 projects worth Rs2,710 crore were sanctioned during Pragati Yatra undertaken by former CM Nitish Kumar.Officials said several major projects are underway at religious destinations. At Punaura Dham in Sitamarhi, a grand temple dedicated to Mata Sita is being constructed at a cost of more than Rs1,000 crore. Vishnupad Temple Corridor in Gaya is being developed at an estimated cost of Rs2,500 crore, while Harihar Nath Temple Corridor in Sonepur is being developed with an investment of more than Rs680 crore.Development work is also progressing at Baba Garibnath Temple, Ashok Dham and Ahilyasthan. Officials said the projects are aimed not merely at improving the appearance of religious sites but also at expanding tourist amenities, connectivity, employment and economic activity in surrounding areas.Govt is also planning new tourism infrastructure, including a Buddhist Meditation and Experience Centre in Bodh Gaya at a cost of Rs165 crore, a glass bridge at Matsyagandha Lake in Saharsa and Luv-Kush Park in Valmikinagar.Expansion of five-star hospitality facilities in Patna, Rajgir and Vaishali is also being pursued.Govt is promoting heli-tourism, including proposed aerial tourism services covering Patna Darshan, Nalanda and Valmikinagar. A proposed ropeway connecting Atal Path in Patna with Hariharnath Temple is expected to add another mode of tourist transport.To connect tourism with local livelihoods, around 1,000 rooms at 34 tourist destinations are being developed under Mukhyamantri Homestay Yojana. Beneficiaries can receive financial assistance of up to Rs11 lakh per unit.Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation managing director Nand Kishore said, “AI could significantly change the way tourists experience destinations. articles.summary: Rohtas police arrested five for posing as cops to rob motorists on NH-19 near Sasaram; arms, fake police gear, phones and an SUV seized; probe on.
articles.body: Sasaram: Police on Saturday night arrested five members of a gang accused of posing as police personnel and targeting motorists for robbery and extortion on NH-19. Police recovered two country-made pistols, a police sign board, live cartridges, three mobile phones and an SUV from their possession.According to Sasaram SDPO V Kumar, a tip-off was received around 8 pm on Saturday that a group of suspicious persons had assembled near a fuel station along the highway in an SUV and were allegedly planning a robbery. A special team was subsequently constituted under the leadership of Sasaram-1 SDPO to verify the information and take action.The police team intercepted the vehicle and detained five persons. One of them was allegedly wearing a police inspector’s uniform, another was dressed as a Bihar Police commando, while the remaining three were in civilian clothes. Police said the man wearing a police uniform identified himself as Rajnish Singh, but later he gave his name as Ranjit Singh. The suspects were asked to produce identity cards, but their inability to provide valid identification raised suspicion. Police subsequently arrested all five and seized the vehicle and other items.Police said the SUV was carrying a fake registration number, while another registration number belonging to Uttar Pradesh was also found inside the vehicle. The arrested persons have been identified as Praveen Singh (36) of Konar in Shiv Sagar; Divakar Kumar Singh alias Divakar Maurya (34) of Amav in Kaimur; Birendra Kumar (35) of Bastalwa in Kudra; Ishrar Alam (38) of Bairibandh in Karghar; and Rajnish Kumar (24) of Chhitaratand in Chenari.A case has been registered at Shiv Sagar police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act. articles.summary: Ahmedabad project manager alleges demat fraud: scammer offering I-T notice help accessed ICICI Direct and Zerodha accounts, transferring shares worth Rs 53 lakh.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: A 41-year-old project manager with a corporate firm alleged that he was cheated of shares worth Rs 53 lakh after a man who offered to help him respond to an income tax notice gained access to his demat accounts and transferred the securities to another account. A colleague of the complainant was allegedly cheated of shares worth Rs 17.8 lakh by the same accused.According to the complaint, the project manager received an income tax notice on June 20 regarding discrepancies in his expenditure and was asked to submit supporting documents. He contacted a man whose mobile number he had obtained from his office and shared the notice with him.The complainant alleged that the man asked him to provide his bank statement for the previous year and details of his demat account so that a response to the tax notice could be prepared.The accused allegedly told him that his existing demat account could not generate the required audit statement and advised him to open a new account with Zerodha. After the account was opened, the accused allegedly sought the account numbers and passwords of both demat accounts.The complainant stated that he was told to share the login credentials of his ICICI Direct and newly opened demat accounts so that shares could be sold from one account and purchased through the other.Following the instructions, he allegedly sold all shares held in his ICICI Direct account for about Rs 60 lakh. The accused then allegedly logged into the Zerodha account and purchased shares worth Rs 1.6 crore.On Aug 12, the accused allegedly informed him that OTPs would be sent to his mobile phone and email address for an audit process and asked him to share them. The complainant alleged that he provided both OTPs.The following day, he found that his Zerodha portfolio showed a zero balance. After contacting the brokerage, he allegedly learnt that shares worth Rs 53 lakh had been transferred to another demat account.The project manager later found that another employee of the company had allegedly been duped in a similar manner and had lost shares worth Rs 17.8 lakh. articles.title: Ahmedabad: Retired BHU professor loses Rs 16L in ‘digital arrest’ scam
articles.summary: Retired BHU professor in Ahmedabad loses Rs 16.2 lakh in ‘digital arrest’ scam as fraudsters posing as police and ATS used WhatsApp video calls to extort funds.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: A 73-year-old retired professor who formerly taught at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and now lives at a senior citizen care centre in Ahmedabad allegedly lost Rs 16.2 lakh after cyberfraudsters posing as police and ATS officers subjected him to a prolonged “digital arrest” through WhatsApp video calls.According to an FIR registered with the Cybercrime police on Saturday, the fraud began on Aug 29 when the victim received a call from an unknown number. The caller identified himself as an officer from the Banaras police headquarters and claimed that a mobile number linked to the professor’s Aadhaar had been used to open an ICICI Bank account through which crores of rupees in illegal transactions had allegedly been routed.The caller also accused him of involvement in child pornography and illegal gambling and claimed that a criminal case had been registered against him. The victim, who had earlier lived in Banaras, told the caller that neither the mobile number nor the bank account belonged to him. He was allegedly informed that the matter would be investigated by the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS).Soon afterwards, another caller posing as an ATS inspector contacted him through WhatsApp video calls. The fraudster allegedly told him that ATS personnel would remain in constant touch with him and instructed him not to disclose the matter to anyone.According to the complaint, the fraudsters threatened to arrest him but later offered to conduct the investigation through video calls because of his age. The complainant alleged that he was kept under continuous WhatsApp surveillance and asked to share details and statements of his bank accounts, which he subsequently provided.On Sept 1, the fraudsters allegedly told him that the money in his bank accounts had to be verified by the Reserve Bank of India as part of the investigation. He was instructed to transfer funds to an ICICI Bank account belonging to a trader.The victim allegedly transferred Rs 11 lakh from his Union Bank of India and Bank of Baroda accounts. The next day, he was asked to transfer another Rs 5.2 lakh to a Yes Bank account.The callers allegedly assured him that the money had been deposited with the RBI for verification and would be returned once the investigation was completed. They also sent him what they claimed was an RBI receipt through WhatsApp.On Sept 9, the fraudsters allegedly informed him that the investigation had been completed and shared a purported NIA no-objection certificate. The retired professor realised he had been duped only after the callers stopped responding. articles.title: Rafale procurement to help India set up 2nd production line of combat aircraft: Defence secretary
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Defence secretary and DRDO chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh said on Sunday that the planned Rafale procurement will help India establish a “second
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence secretary and DRDO chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh said on Sunday that the planned Rafale procurement will help India establish a “second production line” of the combat aircraft even as “indigenous LCA Tejas Mark 1A programme will continue”. He also said that Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd is likely to deliver one squadron of LCA MK1A at the end of this year.Speaking at the NDTV Defence Summit, the defence secretary said, “Rafale is a proven aircraft. Bids from MMRA (for 114 Rafale jets) have come from the French side. We have good relations with France. They have agreed to our mandate that they make it in India with significant levels of indigenisation. This would enable us to create a second production line for fighter aircraft in the country, which is why we are going through with it.”However, he clarified that the procurement of additional Rafale aircraft will not come at the expense of India’s indigenous fighter programme. “The indigenous LCA Tejas Mark 1A programme will continue. It will be a spiral development model where we increasingly perfect it, fitting in indigenous radars that are better than global peers alongside indigenous weapons,” Singh said.Giving an update on Tejas Mk1A’s development, the defence secretary said, “HAL has 27 air frames ready, 11 engines from GE have come, other 16 air frames have been fitted with canopy engines and flown. GE has promised four engines per month during this year, so we will get 12 engines in the rest of the year. We will be able to induct at least one squadron of LCA MK1A at the end of the year. Only some residual issues are left. Weapon integration is almost done... with radar, there are still performance-related issues that are being tackled. HAL has promised 24 LCAs every year thereafter. We hope to get 83 LCAs and 97 jets as part of the second order by 2033.”On problems faced by the IAF when he came to the defence ministry, Singh said, “When I first came to the ministry, the Air Force had three major concerns: depleting size of the fighter fleet and multipliers like AEW&C aircraft and refuellers. All three gaps are on the way to being filled. It won’t happen overnight, but once contracts are signed, delivery expectations are locked in.” On the AMCA project, Singh said the first prototype of AMCA will fly in Sept 2028, hopefully”.

articles.title: With Asian silver, Toor joins Punjab’s elite medal winners
articles.summary: Tejinderpal Singh Toor wins Asian Games shot put silver in Japan, earning third consecutive medal and joining Punjab’s elite multi-medalists.
articles.body: Bathinda: Shot putter Tejinderpal Singh Toor won the silver medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, joining an elite club of Punjab athletes who have won three or more medals across three or fewer consecutive Asian games.Toor, a 31-year-old Punjab Police DSP hailing from Khosa Pando village in Moga district, previously captured gold medals in the 2018 (Jakarta) and 2022 (Hangzhou) Asian Games. His personal best throw of 21.77 metres was set at the 2023 National Games.In the final, Toor recorded a best effort of 20.64 metres to finish behind Iran’s Mohammadreza Tayebise, who clinched gold with a 20.81-metre throw. Expressing disappointment over missing a third straight gold, Toor admitted he had aimed to throw closer to the 21-metre mark.Toor’s sporting career has been marked by personal sacrifice. During the 2018 Jakarta Games, his father, Karam Singh, was critically ill with a cancerous chest tumour. Hours before Toor returned to his village on Sept 4, 2018, to present his first gold medal, his father passed away.With this silver, Toor joins an elite group of legendary multi-medal athletes from Punjab. He shares the distinction with shot put and discus icon Parduman Singh, who won five medals—including three gold, one silver, and one bronze—across the 1954, 1958, and 1962 Games. Legendary sprinter Milkha Singh achieved four gold medals across two consecutive Asian Games in 1958 and 1962, dominating the 200m, 400m, and 4x400m relay events. Fellow shot putter Joginder Singh earned three medals, including two gold and one bronze, between 1962 and 1970, while ace wrestler Kartar Singh secured three medals—two gold and one silver in the 90kg and 100kg categories—across the 1978, 1982, and 1986 Games. articles.title: Preparations in full swing for All India Sub-Junior Ranking Badminton tournament in Jaipur; national women umpires’ seminar from Sept 27
articles.summary: Preparations underway for Yonex-Sunrise All India Sub-Junior (U-15/U-17) Ranking Badminton in Jaipur, Oct 1-9; women umpires’ seminar starts Sept 27.
articles.body: Jaipur: Preparations are in full swing for the Yonex-Sunrise All India Sub-Junior Ranking Badminton tournament, to be held at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur. The competition will feature matches for boys and girls in the Under-15 and U-17 age groups. Singles, doubles, and mixed doubles events will be played in both categories. The competition will be held from October 1 to 9.The Rajasthan Badminton Association and organising secretary KK Sharma stated that eight Yonex courts have arrived in Pink City for the nine-day long tourney. The laying of the courts at the indoor stadium will be completed on Monday. The competition will be played on a total of 19 courts, including 11 in the badminton hall.Before the competition, a seminar for women umpires will begin on September 27, Monday. In all 46 umpires from across the country have reached the Pink City to participate in the seminar.For the seminar, technical officials of the Badminton Association of India, joint convener Rajesh Kamal, chairperson of the technical committee S Muralidharan, World Badminton Federation’s Fine C Dathan, who has umpired in the Tokyo Olympics, experienced badminton umpire Rajiv Mehta, senior Asian umpire Ballerina and Ravi Dixit have reached Jaipur.
